P001.text: Treat the intake-to-permission process as a dynamic system.

P002.text: Its candidate input is usable training capacity at a specified stage; its outputs are stage completions, permissions granted and waiting queues over time.

P003.text: Before intervention, reconcile current cases across the spreadsheets using minimal identifiers and necessary dates.

P004.text: Establish each applicant’s last completed prerequisite, next required step, waiting duration and known availability. Mark missing information as unknown. Offer clarification through existing contact arrangements, respect declined contact and do not classify silence as withdrawal. Record the initial queues, scheduled capacity, cancellations and maintenance commitments; monthly totals alone cannot establish these initial conditions.

P005.text: First observe the existing process at a fixed daily or weekly cadence, including prospective arrivals and transitions, to identify where eligible, available applicants accumulate.

P006.text: If training capacity appears limiting, propose a known step increase at that stage, beginning on a recorded date while keeping safety requirements and other arrangements unchanged where feasible.

P007.text: A sustained step requires an explicit assumption that an evening slot can recur at a fixed frequency; confirm this and instructor and maintenance feasibility before proceeding.

P008.text: Allocate the first evening slot to the stage with the largest documented capacity-related waiting burden that the slot can serve.

P009.text: Hold the second unallocated during a predefined observation period spanning several normal scheduling cycles, if feasible.

P010.text: Record planned and actually delivered capacity separately.

P011.text: If the two evenings are one-off opportunities, treat them as finite pulses and observe their aftermath rather than claiming a sustained-step experiment.

P012.text: If communication or unmet prerequisites dominate, address the documented obstacle first and establish a new baseline before testing capacity.

P013.text: Track trajectories from before the change through the initial response and later behavior: eligible queue size and age at each stage, completions per interval, permissions per interval, cancellations and time to the next required step.

P015.text: Look for delay before additional completions appear, the rate of queue reduction, temporary completion peaks, repeated backlog growth and reduction, downstream queue buildup, and any sustained change or settling.

P016.text: Separate waits associated with unavailable sessions, missing prerequisites, known applicant availability and unresolved communication; allow overlapping or unknown causes.

P017.text: Record concurrent changes in applications, instructor availability, equipment readiness and maintenance so apparent responses can be checked against disturbances.

P018.text: A sustained reduction in eligible waiting after delivered capacity increases, followed by increased permissions, would support capacity limitation at the tested stage under the observed conditions.

P019.text: Faster stage completion followed by downstream accumulation would support a bottleneck shift.

P020.text: Additional places remaining unused while waiting persists would motivate checking availability, communication and prerequisites; it would not establish a single cause.

P021.text: Compare these candidate explanations against the full trajectory, including response delays.

P022.text: Allocate the second evening to the same stage only if eligible demand remains and downstream training and maintenance can absorb it; allocate it downstream if the observed queue transfer and instructor availability support that choice.

P023.text: If no capacity-related benefit is distinguishable, retain the slot pending targeted clarification or a separately observed intervention.

P024.text: A one-off pulse can inform immediate slot usefulness but cannot establish a sustained capacity effect.

P025.text: This is a proposed procedure, not an observed result.

P026.text: Missing dates, uncertain initial queues, small numbers, selective participation, changing demand, cancellations and interacting process changes weaken attribution.

P027.text: Equipment limits, instructor fatigue and maintenance displacement can saturate capacity or make responses nonlinear.

P028.text: Results depend on the equipment, applicants, season and capacity level tested.

P029.text: Define the observation horizon and safety and maintenance guardrails before starting; stop or reduce added capacity if required instruction, equipment checks or necessary maintenance cannot be maintained.

P030.text: Never grant access to accelerate an output measure.

P031.text: If observation ends before the transient resolves, report the trajectory as incomplete and continue monitoring where feasible rather than declaring equilibrium or no effect.

P032.text: Collect only information needed to arrange access and cease further contact when an applicant declines.
